title: Procedural Growth, Bento Composer, Clamp & Reveal, Pressure Press, Exclusive Accordion
description: Arc-length seeded procedural geometry, a collision-swapping bento builder, native line-clamp, real pointer-pressure interactions, and a zero-JS exclusive accordion.

drops.title: Procedural Growth
drops.description: Shapes seed at even arc-length spacing along a drawn stroke and grow in from a shared clock instead of per-shape timers.
drops.concept: Reimplements the distance-based growth model from a Three.js/WebGPU procedural-geometry article: each instance stores a birth distance and grows as (globalClock - birth) / growWindow, eased with an overshoot curve. A reveal slider scrubs visibility by seed rank without regenerating any geometry.
drops.source: Inspired by 'Exploring Procedural Geometry with Three.js and WebGPU' (Codrops)

interaction.mouse: Draw a stroke to seed shapes; sliders tune speed/density/reveal
interaction.click: Pick a shape, or auto-draw a demo spiral
interaction.touch: Draw with a finger; pinch not required

drops.title: Bento Composer
drops.description: Drag any card onto another to swap places on a 6-column bento grid, with live collision detection and no drag-and-drop library.
drops.concept: Recreates the drag-to-swap interaction from a bento grid generator: pointer drag reports the element currently under the cursor via elementFromPoint, and dropping over another card swaps their DOM position directly — the CSS grid handles reflow for free.

interaction.mouse: Drag a card onto another to swap; click the resize icon to cycle its size
interaction.click: Shuffle or reset the layout from the panel

drops.title: Clamp & Reveal
drops.description: Article cards truncate with the native line-clamp property and expand with a real animated height via calc-size(auto, size).
drops.concept: Uses the standardized CSS line-clamp property (rather than the older -webkit-box/-webkit-line-clamp hack) to cap text at N lines, then animates open to the box's true intrinsic height with calc-size(auto, size) plus interpolate-size — something plain CSS transitions couldn't do before calc-size shipped.
drops.source: Inspired by the CSS line-clamp specification (MDN)

interaction.mouse: Drag the line-count slider; click Read more to expand a card
interaction.touch: Tap Read more on any card

drops.title: Pressure Press
drops.description: Reads real PointerEvent.pressure from a stylus or force-capable trackpad, and ramps a simulated pressure on hold for mouse and touch.
drops.concept: Detects genuine hardware pressure (stylus, or a mouse reporting a non-default 0.5 value) and drives a squish button, a force meter, and a pressure-sensitive brush stroke directly from it; on ordinary hardware it falls back to a hold-duration ramp so the interaction still feels alive.
drops.source: Inspired by stuyam/pressure (Force Touch / Pointer Pressure library)

interaction.mouse: Press and hold any of the three demos; pressure ramps the longer you hold
interaction.click: Tap to squish the button instantly
interaction.touch: Hold with a finger, or use a stylus for real pressure

drops.title: Exclusive Accordion
drops.description: A FAQ list built from plain details elements — grouping them by name makes the browser enforce exclusivity for you.
drops.concept: Every <details> sharing a name attribute joins a group where opening one automatically closes the others, entirely natively. Pairs it with ::details-content and calc-size(auto, size) for an animated open/close instead of the usual instant snap.
drops.source: Inspired by Bramus's 'Styling <details>: Horizontal Accordion' (CodePen) and the details name exclusive-accordion feature

interaction.mouse: Click a question to expand it; toggle the mode buttons to compare behavior
interaction.click: Switch between independent and exclusive grouping
